name: pscalib-pr-merge-cycle.SETUP
purpose: The fourth file of the pscalib-pr-merge-cycle campaign set, and the single place where machine- and site-dependent facts live. The contract references keys in this file instead of pasting absolute paths, hostnames or usernames, so the contract stays readable on a machine that has never touched SLAC. Read this BEFORE issuing any remote command.
campaign_set: .goal/pscalib-pr-merge-cycle.ledger.json   the ledger (may hold a run in progress)
relation_to_earlier_campaigns: Written for pscalib-pr-merge-cycle, but every remote fact here applies equally to pscalib-calib-speedup and pscalib-numpy-only-8x, which carry their own SETUP.md files. Those two are the historical record of what each campaign assumed at the time and must not be edited. Where they disagree with this file about a LIVE remote fact, this file is newer — its remote, tools, paths and repo blocks were re-verified first-hand on 2026-08-06.
how_to_reference: The contract cites keys as SETUP.<key>, where SETUP means this file — e.g. SETUP.paths.candidate_worktree_numpy. Resolve a path as paths.project_root + '/' + the relative value under paths._relative_to_project_root. Retargeting the whole set to a different user, project or site requires editing exactly ONE value: paths.project_root.

verified.what: Every entry under remote, tools, paths and repo was re-checked first-hand on 2026-08-06 from a fresh bridge session. The remote is shared and mutable — re-run verification.command rather than trusting this table on a later date.
verified.command: for t in rg fd gcc python3 uv gh git; do command -v $t; done; ls ~/bridge-server; for p in <every resolved paths value>; do [ -e "$p" ] && echo OK $p || echo MISS $p; done

remote.invariant: The host is fixed for these campaigns and nothing runs locally. A number measured on this login node is a SMOKE TEST ONLY — it is shared and this workload is memory-bandwidth bound, so login-node timings are noisy and pessimistic and are not comparable to any baseline.

local_preconditions.note: Both must hold before iteration 1. Neither is fixable by an agent — one needs a package install, the other an interactive MFA prompt. If either fails, report the blocker plainly, ask the user to resolve it, and stop. Do not work around it and do not mark any done_when item met on a machine that cannot reach the remote.

cc_bridge_cli.on_failure: the cc-bridge CLI is not installed here; there is no fallback. The bridge skill is /bridge-skills.

ssh_non_interactive.check: timeout 25 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15 sdfiana025 hostname
ssh_non_interactive.why_batchmode: fails fast instead of hanging on a password or MFA prompt
ssh_non_interactive.on_failure: MFA is the common case on a fresh machine. S3DF requires it through the jump host and it cannot be automated. Ask the user to type `! ssh s3dflogin-mfa.slac.stanford.edu` in the prompt so the output lands in the conversation.

diagnosis.Permission denied (publickey): no key, or key not registered at SLAC

local_preconditions.cwd: Run /goal from the directory that CONTAINS .goal/. The contract's ledger and claims paths are relative, so a different cwd writes them somewhere unintended and the printed digest silently stops matching the file on disk. The name of the containing directory does not matter.

ssh_config.note: What ~/.ssh/config must contain on the machine you run from. Substitute your own SLAC username for remote.user. A different machine may additionally need IdentityFile.
ssh_config.controlmaster: A ControlMaster socket under ~/.ssh/sockets makes repeat connections fast and avoids re-prompting for MFA. An optimisation, not a requirement — but if it exists and is live, connections are near-instant, which is a useful signal that auth is already established.

bridge.root_dir: Use --root-dir /sdf (wide). A narrow root only restricts `bridge read` paths; absolute paths inside `bridge bash` work regardless, so a narrow root buys nothing and costs you reads.
bridge.session_naming: Each campaign uses its own prefix so sessions never collide across campaigns: pscalib-* (pscalib-calib-speedup), pscalib2-* (pscalib-numpy-only-8x), pscalib3-* (pscalib-pr-merge-cycle, this one). Never a human-style name (s1, s2) and never another campaign's prefix.
bridge.why_fresh: Start your own and inherit none. A leftover session may have a different --root-dir, be stale, or be in use, and sessions serialize — so sharing one silently blocks your commands behind another caller's. One session runs one command at a time, so three is the parallelism ceiling. Stop all of yours when the iteration ends.
bridge.stopping_others: A leftover session with a CAMPAIGN prefix is infrastructure and may be stopped. Never stop one with a human-style name.
gotchas: --timeout goes BEFORE the subcommand: `bridge --timeout 600 bash "..."`, never `bridge bash --timeout 600`.
Two independent timeouts: the remote one above, and the local Bash tool's own 120 s. For anything long, redirect to a remote file and poll it.
Output caps at 1 MB. Scope rg/fd or redirect and filter remotely.
A command that returns instantly with no output is a QUOTING ERROR, not a negative result. Re-check before believing an absence.
The remote /bin/sh does not support process substitution `<(...)`. Use temp files.

cautions: /sdf/scratch is PURGEABLE — never leave the only copy of anything there.
/sdf/data/lcls/ds contains both lower- and upper-case hutch directories (mfx and MFX), which inflates any sweep that does not account for it.
Write nothing outside project_root and the local campaign directory. Never write to another user's /sdf tree.

repo.gh_auth: authenticated as carbonscott, scopes include repo and workflow
repo.gh_known_defect: gh 2.62.0's `gh pr edit` exits 1 on this repo because it queries the deprecated Projects-classic projectCards GraphQL field. It prints only a warning, so the failure is easy to miss — ALWAYS re-fetch the body to confirm an edit landed. Working alternative: gh api -X PATCH /repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N> -F body=@<file>

tools.note: Paths verified 2026-08-06. gh, fd, uv and python3 are user-installed under remote.home/.local; rg, gcc and git are system.

measurement_env.where: milano nodes via slurm (sdfmilan*), 120 CPU / 503 GiB, --exclusive. NOT the login node.
rules: 512 events, never 128. At 128 events bit-identical code produced ratios of 4.31x and 1.33x depending on arm order, driven by page-cache warming.

Serialize your own jobs and check node exclusivity before submitting. Three runs in the first campaign were destroyed by an I/O storm from that campaign's own concurrent xtc readers. --exclusive protects the CPUs, not Weka.

Check arm symmetry by BYTES READ, never by MB_per_s. MB_per_s is nbytes/wall with nbytes fixed by the event count, so an MB/s symmetry rule is a wall-time symmetry test in disguise and any real speedup above ~1.18x must fail it.
Re-measure the denominator in the same job. Anchoring on a baseline from a prior job produced a 33% unexplained incumbent-arm slowdown that nobody could account for.
BENCH_WORKERS is read from the env and split on COMMA, so BENCH_WORKERS='1 16' kills the harness before argparse — unset it.
measurement_env.not_needed_for_every_campaign: The three-conjunct bit gate is psana-free, runs on paths.fixture, and needs no node allocation. A campaign that changes no compute path needs no slurm time at all.

unowned_code.finding: The benchmark harness at paths.harness is NOT under version control — `git rev-parse` in its directory reports no repo (verified 2026-08-06).
unowned_code.consequence: There is no upstream to contribute the harness patch to. The patcher script and a written-up pattern are the only durable homes for it, which is why the numpy campaign shipped docs/fast-event-loops.md plus an extra/ archive rather than an upstream PR.

failure_modes.bridge status shows no active session: you have not started one; start one, do not hunt for someone else's
failure_modes.bridge-session start fails, 3 already ru: at the session cap; stop one of yours or a leftover campaign-prefixed one
failure_modes.ssh hangs with no output: MFA needed; stop and ask the user to log in
failure_modes.bridge bash returns instantly and empty: quoting error, not an empty result
failure_modes.bridge bash output truncated: hit the 1 MB cap; redirect and filter remotely
failure_modes.command killed at ~120 s: local Bash timeout; background it remotely and poll a file
failure_modes.slurm job pending indefinitely: queue contention; record the job id and poll, do not resubmit blind
failure_modes.timings ~3x worse than baseline: measured on the login node; re-run under srun on milano
failure_modes.ValueError before argparse: BENCH_WORKERS is set and split on commas; unset it
failure_modes.gh pr edit prints a warning and changes: the Projects-classic defect; use the gh api PATCH form and re-fetch to confirm

not_verified: The ssh_config block reflects what worked on the authoring machine; a different machine may need IdentityFile or a different jump-host alias. Whether CI exists on the pscalib repo, and whether any of its test suite runs off-SLAC, has never been checked — most tests require psana, which is a SLAC production conda build and not pip-installable.
